hook: MIT engineers used sewn cotton molds to slash concrete usage and halve steel requirements today.

sections.voiceover: MIT engineers used sewn cotton molds to slash concrete usage and halve steel requirements today.
sections.visual_cue: MIT engineers using fabric molds to cut concrete and steel usage

sections.voiceover: MIT engineers built a 3-meter concrete test beam using a sewn cotton mold, requiring one-third the amount of concrete and half as much steel as a conventional beam.
sections.visual_cue: MIT engineers building a concrete beam with a sewn cotton mold

sections.voiceover: Yet, the deflection of the beam still matched within about 2 percent of the computer model predictions.
sections.visual_cue: MIT engineers checking the deflection of the beam

sections.voiceover: This method used one-third the concrete and half the steel, yet deflection still matched the model predictions.
sections.visual_cue: MIT engineers showing the beam with a computer model comparison

sections.voiceover: MIT engineers' method could bring material-saving concrete beams within reach.
